html:
Rajputana, the land of the Rajputs, is the region of today's Rajasthan and its edges. On the 1530 and 1600 maps it is the age when the Rajput kingdoms were drawn into the Mughal Empire. The name itself came later, from British writers around 1800.

After Babur beat Rana Sanga in 1527, the Rajputs were weakened but not conquered. Akbar chose alliance over war where he could. In 1562 he married a princess of Amber, and her nephew Man Singh became one of his top generals. Many Rajput kings joined the Mughal nobility and kept their own lands.

Mewar refused. Akbar stormed its fortress of Chittor in 1568. Maharana Pratap fought on from the hills and met a Mughal army under Man Singh at the Battle of Haldighati in 1576. Mewar finally made peace with Jahangir in 1615. For the century before, see Rajasthan around 1500; for later, the Rajput states.
